questions.q: Which of these is NOT an elevator or escalator manufacturer?
questions.ref: General mechanical, electrical, and fire-protection practice (HVAC, PEC)
questions.n: Honeywell makes building controls and fire alarms. The recall's key lists Kone as an elevator maker.

questions.q: What is the commonly specified minimum lap splice length for reinforcing bars?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: A splice overlaps two bars so force passes between them. Memory trick: 40 db and 600 mm.

questions.q: Which insulation has the lowest R-value on its own but performs well when paired with an air cavity?
questions.ref: General building-insulation practice and R-value references
questions.n: Foil reflects radiant heat but only works with a still air gap. Like a mirror that needs space to bounce.

questions.q: What is the standard electrical frequency in the Philippines?
questions.ref: General mechanical, electrical, and fire-protection practice (HVAC, PEC)
questions.n: The recall listed 220 V 60 Hz; the PEC states 230 V, 60 Hz. Remember frequency: 60 Hz.

questions.q: What concrete cover is commonly specified for a suspended slab?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: Suspended slabs are inside the building and away from earth, so the thinnest cover applies.

questions.q: Which insulation seals both air and moisture when sprayed onto a wall?
questions.ref: General building-insulation practice and R-value references
questions.n: Spray foam expands and fills every gap, like caulk that also insulates.

questions.q: Which survey re-establishes lost property corners or monuments using the title's technical description?
questions.ref: General land-surveying practice
questions.n: Re-locating = finding the original boundary again. Setting-out marks new design points on site.

questions.q: Which footing suits adobe soil (a hard volcanic tuff with high bearing capacity)?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: Adobe is strong, so each column can have its own simple pad. Word root: adobe from Arabic at-tub, 'the brick'.

questions.q: Which timber is classed among the 'Philippine mahoganies'?
questions.ref: General building-materials and finishing references (timber, paints, gypsum, flooring, hardware)
questions.n: Yakal and guijo are hard, heavy structural timbers. Tanguile is the lighter lauan-type wood.

questions.q: In a two-chamber septic tank, where does the clarified liquid go after the second chamber?
o: To the settling/leaching chamber or leaching field
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines and the Code on Sanitation (PD 856) IRR, Chapter XVII
questions.n: Chamber 1 is the digestion chamber where solids are broken down; chamber 2 lets the liquid settle, then it leaches to the ground. The recall offered 'digestive' and 'leaching' for the second chamber, so choose leaching.

questions.q: What is the function of a base plate?
o: Spreads the column load onto the concrete foundation
Connects the beam to the roof
questions.ref: General structural-steel and roof-framing practice (AISC/NSCP slenderness limits)
questions.n: A small column load becomes a big load on a tiny spot, so the plate spreads it like a snowshoe. The recall option said 'connect column to beam', which is wrong.

questions.q: What does VOC mean in paint?
questions.ref: General building-materials and finishing references (timber, paints, gypsum, flooring, hardware)
questions.n: Word root: volatile from Latin volare, 'to fly', because it evaporates into the air. Low-VOC paint has less smell and fumes.

questions.q: What do you do before installing plumbing fixtures?
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines and the Code on Sanitation (PD 856) IRR, Chapter XVII
questions.n: Roughing-in installs the hidden pipes first. Think of laying the skeleton before dressing the body.

questions.q: What is the maximum slenderness ratio for compression members in steel?
questions.ref: General structural-steel and roof-framing practice (AISC/NSCP slenderness limits)
questions.n: Slenderness ratio = KL/r. Compression: 200; tension: 300. A very slender compression member buckles like a thin straw.

questions.q: Which is a gypsum board brand in the Philippines?
questions.ref: General building-materials and finishing references (timber, paints, gypsum, flooring, hardware)
questions.n: Mapei makes tile adhesives, Phelps Dodge wires, and Kone elevators.

questions.q: Where is the best location for utility openings (sleeves) through a beam?
o: At the top of the beam over the column
Right next to the support at the bottom
Middle third of the span at mid-depth
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: Shear is highest near supports, so avoid cutting there. Mid-depth is near the neutral axis, where bending stress is lowest. The recall options were cut off, so this is the standard rule.

questions.q: What is the spacing of vertical and horizontal bars in a CHB wall?
o: 600 mm vertical; horizontal every 3 layers of CHB
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: Three CHB layers equal about 600 mm, so both grids are 600 mm.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a threshold?
o: Seals the gap at the door bottom and smooths the floor change
questions.ref: General building-materials and finishing references (timber, paints, gypsum, flooring, hardware)
questions.n: A threshold is the strip you step over, closing the door gap.

questions.q: Which slab type carries heavy loads without beams?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: The slab sits directly on columns and gets thicker drop panels at the columns.

questions.q: Which roof has two slopes?
questions.ref: General roofing practice (gables, hips, flashing, gutters)
questions.n: Gable has two slopes meeting at a ridge, like an open book on a table. A hip roof slopes on four sides. Word root: gable from Old Norse gafl.

questions.q: Which HVAC device reduces noise in ductwork?
questions.ref: General mechanical, electrical, and fire-protection practice (HVAC, PEC)
questions.n: Word root: attenuate from Latin attenuare, 'to make thin'. It thins out the noise. A plenum is a space full of air (Latin plenum, 'full').

questions.q: Which admixture reduces the water needed in a concrete mix?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: Word root: Greek plastikos, 'moldable'. It makes the mix flow with less water, like adding oil to a stiff dough.

questions.q: What is the typical order of layers for a tropical roof (from the top down)?
o: Roof sheet, then purlins, then insulation
Insulation, then purlins, then roof sheet
Purlins, then roof sheet, then insulation
Roof sheet, then insulation, then purlins
questions.ref: General building-insulation practice and R-value references
questions.n: The insulation sits just under the roof sheets, over the purlins, so heat is stopped near the top. Word root: insulate from Latin insula, 'island', as in cut off.

questions.q: Which is a Philippine electrical wire brand?
questions.ref: General mechanical, electrical, and fire-protection practice (HVAC, PEC)
questions.n: Phelps Dodge makes building wire. Others are gypsum, adhesives, and elevators.

questions.q: What concrete cover is required where concrete is deposited directly against earth?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: Earth contact is the harshest, so the cover is the thickest. 50 mm applies where concrete is exposed to earth but cast against forms.

questions.q: Which is the cheapest insulation for tropical buildings?
questions.ref: General building-insulation practice and R-value references
questions.n: In the tropics, radiant heat from the roof is the main enemy, and foil blocks it cheaply.

questions.q: Which way should an emergency exit door swing?
o: Outward, in the direction of exit travel
questions.ref: General mechanical, electrical, and fire-protection practice (HVAC, PEC)
questions.n: In a rush, people push forward. An outward door opens with the crowd.

questions.q: Which footing is used under a continuous wall?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: A strip runs along the wall like a belt under it.

questions.q: Which insulation is made with about 50% recycled PET material?
questions.ref: General building-insulation practice and R-value references
questions.n: PET is the plastic in drink bottles, so the insulation is recycled bottles.

questions.q: Under the IRR of the Code on Sanitation, what is the minimum distance of a septic tank from any well, spring, or cistern?
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines and the Code on Sanitation (PD 856) IRR, Chapter XVII
questions.n: Keep waste far from drinking water. The National Plumbing Code table shows 15.2 m for well-to-septic, so if your exam offers only 15 or 30, check which code the question names. Word root: cistern from Latin cisterna, from cista, 'box'.

questions.q: Which footing is best for weak soil and flood-prone sites?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: A mat spreads the load over the whole footprint, like snowshoes on soft snow.

questions.q: Which coat is applied on wood to make the lacquer topcoat smooth and easy to sand?
questions.ref: General building-materials and finishing references (timber, paints, gypsum, flooring, hardware)
questions.n: The sealer fills wood pores, like putting primer on a rough canvas. Word root: lacquer traces to Sanskrit laksha, the lac resin.

questions.q: Which unit separates oil and grease from kitchen wastewater, working like a septic tank for fats?
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines and the Code on Sanitation (PD 856) IRR, Chapter XVII
questions.n: Fat floats, water flows out underneath. Think of skimming fat off a soup.

questions.q: What is the function of a shear stud?
o: Connects the steel beam to the concrete slab so they act together
questions.ref: General structural-steel and roof-framing practice (AISC/NSCP slenderness limits)
questions.n: Studs make composite action, so the slab and beam work as one T-shaped beam.

questions.q: Which primer is applied on steel or metal doors before painting?
questions.ref: General building-materials and finishing references (timber, paints, gypsum, flooring, hardware)
questions.n: Red oxide protects steel from rust, like a raincoat before the outer coat.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of water closets that can be served by a circuit vent?
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines and the Code on Sanitation (PD 856) IRR, Chapter XVII
questions.n: A circuit vent serves a row of fixtures with one vent. The recall options were 4, 6, 8, 10.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a sag rod?
o: Tension rod that stops purlins from sagging and deflecting sideways
questions.ref: General structural-steel and roof-framing practice (AISC/NSCP slenderness limits)
questions.n: A sag rod holds the purlin's sideways bend, like a clothesline brace.

questions.q: Which is the cheapest flooring among plastic laminate, terrazzo, and granite?
questions.ref: General building-materials and finishing references (timber, paints, gypsum, flooring, hardware)
questions.n: Terrazzo is poured chips of marble in cement, cheaper than solid stone. Word root: Italian terrazzo, 'terrace'. Plastic laminate is mainly a countertop and wall surface, not a floor choice.

questions.q: By rule of thumb, how should the beam width compare with the column width?
o: Beam width is unrelated to the column
Beam width is smaller than or equal to the column width
Beam width is much wider than the column
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: Strong column, weak beam: if something must yield, let the beam bend first so the column survives.

questions.q: Which vertical bar size is commonly used for a 4-inch CHB wall?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: Thin walls take thin bars. The recall had no clear key between 10 and 12 mm for 4 in, and 12 mm for 8 in; confirm.

questions.q: What is the purpose of weatherstripping?
o: Seals gaps against air, water, and sound
questions.ref: General building-materials and finishing references (timber, paints, gypsum, flooring, hardware)
questions.n: It is a soft seal around the door or window, like a draft seal on a fridge.

questions.q: What is the purpose of reinforcing bars in concrete?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: Concrete is strong when squeezed and weak when stretched, so steel does the stretching job.

questions.q: What is a common mistake in roofing installation?
o: Poor sheet overlap and wrong flashing
questions.ref: General roofing practice (gables, hips, flashing, gutters)
questions.n: Water finds any gap. Flashing is the metal collar that seals roof edges and joints.

questions.q: Which device is installed in a duct to stop fire from spreading through it?
questions.ref: General mechanical, electrical, and fire-protection practice (HVAC, PEC)
questions.n: A fire damper closes when heat is detected, like a trapdoor in the duct. Fire stop seals pipe and cable holes in walls.

questions.q: What is the maximum slump commonly specified for concrete in beams and slabs?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: Slump measures how wet the mix is. Typical Philippine notes use 100 mm max for beams and slabs. The recall options included 125.

questions.q: Where does insulation go for a vaulted ceiling?
questions.ref: General building-insulation practice and R-value references
questions.n: A vaulted ceiling is the roof, so the insulation follows the slope of the roof.

questions.q: Which is a lower-cost circuit breaker brand among Koten, GE, and Square D?
questions.ref: General mechanical, electrical, and fire-protection practice (HVAC, PEC)
questions.n: Breakers range in cost by brand. This is from the recall and is a market fact, so check local prices.

questions.q: What concrete cover is commonly specified for a slab on grade?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: Typical Philippine notes use 40 mm for slab on grade and 20 mm for suspended slabs. The recall options differed slightly, so check your reviewer.

questions.q: Which insulation is more resistant to water vapor, EPS or XPS?
questions.ref: General building-insulation practice and R-value references
questions.n: XPS has a denser, closed cell structure, like a tight sponge versus a loose one.

questions.q: Which survey locates utilities, roads, and natural and built features of a site?
questions.ref: General land-surveying practice
questions.n: Word root: topography from Greek topos, 'place' + graphein, 'to write', so 'writing the place'.

questions.q: Which footing is connected to another footing by a beam?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: The strap beam is a handle joining two footings.

questions.q: What does S2S mean for lumber?
questions.ref: General building-materials and finishing references (timber, paints, gypsum, flooring, hardware)
questions.n: S4S is surfaced on four sides. Rough lumber is unsurfaced.

questions.q: Under the Sanitation Code IRR, what is the minimum distance between a cistern and a septic tank?
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines and the Code on Sanitation (PD 856) IRR, Chapter XVII
questions.n: A cistern stores clean water, so it gets the same 25 m buffer as a well.

questions.q: Which describes a Lally column?
o: A steel tube column filled with concrete
questions.ref: General structural-steel and roof-framing practice (AISC/NSCP slenderness limits)
questions.n: Named after John Lally, its inventor. Concrete inside stops the steel tube from buckling.

questions.q: Which paint type is oil-based?
questions.ref: General building-materials and finishing references (timber, paints, gypsum, flooring, hardware)
questions.n: Word root: alkyd from alcohol + acid. Emulsion comes from Latin emulgere, 'to milk out', and is water-based.

questions.q: What does PVC stand for?
questions.ref: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines and the Code on Sanitation (PD 856) IRR, Chapter XVII
questions.n: Word root: vinyl from Latin vinum, 'wine' (a chemistry link), and chloride from Greek chloros, 'pale green'.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a post base?
o: Connects a wood post to a concrete foundation and keeps it off the ground
questions.ref: General structural-steel and roof-framing practice (AISC/NSCP slenderness limits)
questions.n: It lifts the post bottom above moisture, like a shoe sole.

questions.q: What gypsum board thickness is commonly used for wall partitions?
questions.ref: General building-materials and finishing references (timber, paints, gypsum, flooring, hardware)
questions.n: Walls need stiffer boards than ceilings. 9 mm is common for ceilings.

questions.q: Which part of a simply supported beam has the positive moment, so the main bars go at the bottom?
o: At the top of the beam only
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: A beam sags in the middle, so the bottom stretches and the bottom bars work there. Think of a bent ruler.

questions.q: What is the common standard thickness set for concrete hollow blocks (CHB)?
o: 4 in, 6 in, and 8 in (a 5 in block is not standard)
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: Sizes are 100, 150, and 200 mm. 5 in is the odd one out.

questions.q: Which hardware stops a door from slamming?
questions.ref: General building-materials and finishing references (timber, paints, gypsum, flooring, hardware)
questions.n: A damper slows the door down, like a seat belt for a door. A stopper only stops it at the wall.

questions.q: In a one-way slab, where is the main reinforcement placed?
o: Parallel to the short span (with temperature bars across)
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: A one-way slab spans the short way, like a plank across a narrow stream.

questions.q: Which vertical bar size is commonly used for an 8-inch CHB wall?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: Thicker walls take thicker bars. Recall option was 10 mm or 12 mm; confirm with your reviewer.

questions.q: Which agency regulates noise pollution from industrial buildings?
questions.ref: DENR/EMB regulations (PD 1586 ECC; Clean Air Act and noise standards)
questions.n: DENR through the EMB handles environmental standards, including noise. DENR-EMB also issues ECCs.

questions.q: What binds the sand and gravel together in concrete?
questions.ref: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and common Philippine structural general notes
questions.n: Word root: cement from Latin caementum, 'rough stone chips'. Concrete comes from Latin concretus, 'grown together'. Cement is the glue.

questions.q: What does the size of a roof gutter depend on?
o: The roof area and the rainfall intensity
questions.ref: General roofing practice (gables, hips, flashing, gutters)
questions.n: More roof and more rain means more water, so a bigger gutter. Word root: gutter from Old French goutiere, from goute, 'drop'.
